unmapped_findings: The solution-treated (parent-state) 17Al alloy had a Vickers hardness of 259.8 ± 1.5 HV, which serves as the common baseline for all 17Al aging conditions including the 625 °C/1 h sample.

For the 17Al alloy, aging at 625 °C produced a nearly time-independent hardness plateau of ~813–878 HV across 1–10 h (813.0 ± 20.8 HV at 1 h, 872.0 ± 24.4 HV at 3 h, 878.4 ± 28.3 HV at 6 h, 870.5 ± 24.9 HV at 10 h); the peak hardness of the 17Al alloy (924.9 ± 25.8 HV) was instead reached at 575 °C for 6 h, not at 625 °C.

The specific sample (17Al aged at 625 °C for 1 h) is not the peak-hardness state of the 17Al alloy; the nanoindentation measurements (Fig. 13) and TEM observations (Fig. 12) of the 17Al alloy were performed on the 575 °C/6 h peak-hardness sample, and the XRD trace for 17Al (Fig. 10) was measured on the 575 °C/1 h sample, so those results do not directly correspond to this 625 °C/1 h sample.
